# Claim Lifecycle Management

Claim Lifecycle Management refers to overseeing dental insurance claims from submission through final reimbursement. It begins when a clinic submits a claim for services rendered, including codes for procedures, patient details, and billed amounts. The insurer reviews, adjudicates, and either approves or denies the claim. Approved claims proceed to payment; denied claims require follow-up or resubmission.

Tradeoffs include balancing thorough documentation to reduce denials against administrative time spent on claim corrections. Efficient management improves cash flow and chair utilization by minimizing billing delays.

Example: A $500 root canal claim is submitted. The insurer approves $450 after adjustments; $450 is received in 30 days. A $50 denial triggers a resubmission with additional documentation, resolving in 15 more days.

Common failures stem from coding errors, missing info, or untimely submissions causing delays or denials.
